item.title: Top 10 Central Bank Gold Reserves
item.description: Global central banks own about 17 percent of all the gold ever mined, with reserves topping 36,520.7 metric tons (MT) at the end of November 2025. They acquired the vast majority after becoming net buyers of the metal in 2010.Central banks purchase gold for a number of reasons: to mitigate risk, to hedge against inflation and to promote economic stability.
